fix(linux): prevent AppImage crashes by disabling DMABUF

This addresses a critical crash (EGL_BAD_PARAMETER) observed on Fedora
and other modern Linux distributions when running the AppImage.

The crash is caused by a version mismatch between the AppImage's bundled
libraries and the host system's newer graphics drivers when attempting
hardware acceleration (DMABUF).

Changes:
- Detects if running as an AppImage via the APPIMAGE env var.
- Sets WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1 only for AppImage execution,
  forcing compatibility mode while preserving full GPU acceleration for
  native (.deb/.rpm) builds.
- Reordered logger initialization to ensuring startup logs are captured.
- Removed duplicate 	auri_plugin_shell initialization.

security: harden path validation and restrict Tauri capabilities

   This commit implements multiple security hardening measures to reduce
   attack surface and mitigate potential vulnerabilities.

   Path Traversal Prevention

   Enhanced `validate_path_component()` in receive.rs and
   main_reference.rs:
   - Block empty path components
   - Block backslash characters (Windows path traversal)
   - Block parent directory traversal (..)
   - Block current directory references (.)
   - Block null byte injection (path truncation attacks)

   Previously only forward slashes were blocked, leaving the application
   vulnerable to directory traversal attacks on received files.

   Tauri Capability Restrictions

   Shell Permissions
   - Removed `shell:allow-open` from default.json and sendme.json
   - Prevents arbitrary URL/file opening via system handlers

   HTTP Allowlist
   - Restricted from wildcard (`https://*:*`, `http://*:*`) to
     `https://github.com/**`
   - Mitigates SSRF risks and limits outbound request destinations
   - Enforces HTTPS-only communication

   Asset Protocol Scope
   - Removed overly permissive `"allow": ["**/*"]` wildcard
   - Enabled `requireLiteralLeadingDot: true` for hidden file protection
   - Limits filesystem access through the asset protocol

   Dependency Updates
   - Updated package-lock.json and Cargo.lock

fix(send): skip invalid path components instead of failing share

  WalkDir traverses everything including build sysroots with systemd
  unit files containing literal backslashes (e.g.
  `system-systemd\x2dcryptsetup.slice`).
  Previously this failed the entire share operation.

  Now logs warning and skips invalid files, fails only if no valid files
  remain.

feat(nearby): allow gated identity probes from unpaired peers

Widens the control-connection handshake gate to accept unpaired peers
under Discoverability::Everyone, and unifies the paired/unpaired
control dispatch loop so both can be served WhoAreYou probes (subject
to should_answer_identity) while unpaired peers are otherwise
restricted to unpaired_message_allowed message types.

fix(nearby): keep paired sessions intact across identity probes

- Register/unregister the control session with paired_connections
  lazily, on the first message that implies an ongoing relationship
  (anything but WhoAreYou), so a probe-only connection to an
  already-paired peer never clobbers the entry their real persistent
  control connection occupies.
- A paired peer's refused WhoAreYou (Discoverability::Off) now ignores
  the probe instead of closing the whole session; only unpaired
  connections still get closed on refusal.
- set_discoverability now awaits the access-state write directly
  instead of firing a detached task, so callers observe the new
  policy deterministically.

feat(nearby): discover local devices over mDNS

Adds lan_discovery.rs, the only module that touches multicast, and wires
its LanEvent stream into NodeService: sightings feed NearbyRegistry and
spawn identity probes, expirations clear stale entries, and a paired
peer's reappearance nudges its reconnect backoff instead of waiting it
out. Discovery starts/stops with the Discoverability setting and never
fails node startup — a failed mDNS pump is logged and surfaced as
nearby-unavailable.

fix(nearby): stop mDNS advertising on discoverability Off via endpoint rebuild

iroh 1.0.3 can't unregister an address-lookup service from a live endpoint,
and MdnsAddressLookup's advertise flag is fixed at construction, so the
previous stop/start toggle never actually silenced the mDNS broadcast and
leaked one live actor per Off/On cycle. Discoverability transitions across
the Off boundary now share reconfigure_network's endpoint-rebuild path:
close the old endpoint, drop the old MdnsAddressLookup clone, and only
register a new one when the setting calls for it. reconfigure_network
itself now also restarts LAN discovery on the rebuilt endpoint instead of
stranding it. The nearby list is cleared only after the old consumer task
is confirmed stopped, so no in-flight event can repopulate it.

Also normalizes an old-build peer's empty os reply to None instead of
storing Some(""), at the probe-to-registry boundary in spawn_identity_probe.

fix(nearby): serialize network rebuild transitions

reconfigure_network and set_discoverability both close/rebuild the
endpoint and lan_discovery, but nothing serialized concurrent calls: two
overlapping invocations could interleave their close/build steps (one
closing the endpoint the other just built), and each caller's
Off-boundary decision could go stale before its registry clear/discovery
start ran against the wrong state.

Add a network_transition mutex held for the whole decide-then-rebuild-
then-settle sequence in reconfigure_network, set_discoverability, and
shutdown, so only one transition ever touches runtime/lan_discovery at a
time and a caller's post-rebuild decision can't be raced by another.

Also corrects doc comments that overstated abort()'s cancellation
guarantees as synchronous/provable.

records a PairedDevice, drops the peer from the Nearby list, and hands off to
the existing invite-response path; declining with block=true adds the peer to
a new blocked set that the handshake hook now rejects at the QUIC layer.

  unpaired_message_allowed), so a nearby invite's sender can actually learn

  message gate. The receiving side only acts on one that matches an

  immediately after writing, racing the write against the peer ever reading
  it for any freshly-dialed (uncached) connection — now held open briefly in
  the background like deliver_invite already does.

  seeds the Nearby registry the same way a real mDNS sighting would, so the

fix(nearby): stop a nearby accept from unpairing both devices

`accept_nearby_invite` refreshed `paired_connections` — which spawns an
outbound `Recognition` dial — before delivering `InviteResponse::Accepted`.
The sender had not committed its half of the pairing yet, so it closed that
dial with "not permitted for unpaired peer". The acceptor's connect loop
reads that close as a missed `Forget` (`close_implies_remote_unpair`) and
marked the peer `UnpairedRemotely`, dropping it from the allowlist. The
sender then hit the mirror image of the same rejection and unpaired too, so a
successful accept collapsed to "This device removed the pairing" on both ends
within seconds, with the peer reappearing under Nearby as unverified.

Deliver the accept before refreshing, leaving the sender a full connect
handshake to commit before the Recognition arrives.

Only the Nearby paths were affected; the pairing-code flow already commits
the joiner on the host before replying.

under Nearby one row above. The name is already in hand: pass the
`pending_nearby_invites` snapshot as the fallback.

`commit_nearby_pairing` then persisted that same snapshot verbatim. Taken
when the user clicked Pair, it holds a prefix whenever the identity probe had
not answered yet — and the probe commonly lands during the invite round trip.
That prefix became the device's stored name permanently, on the initiator
only, since the acceptor probes at accept time. Prefer whatever Nearby knows
at commit time and keep the snapshot as the fallback.

feat(history): open a transfer's files from its history row

A history row recorded where files were meant to go but offered no way to
get there, and on Android the path it stored was app-private staging — the
copy out to the picked folder or Download/DashBeam happens after the row is
closed, so "Saved to" named a directory the export had just emptied.

The receive now reports its real destination back to history once the export
finishes, storing the SAF tree URI alongside the readable path: an Android
path is a label, not an address, so reopening the exact folder needs the
tree the files went to rather than whatever settings holds now.

Open resolves against the filesystem instead of trusting the record. A lone
surviving file is revealed directly, several are shown in the deepest folder
containing them, and a destination whose files were moved or deleted says so
instead of opening an empty folder.

The row itself becomes one big toggle so a tap anywhere expands it, with
delete moved into the panel behind a confirmation that spells out when

transfer was about to be dropped.

The lifecycle moves into a store shared by all three surfaces — the corner
banner, the settings-sidebar alert and the settings panel — so they cannot
disagree or start two downloads of the same release. Download progress is
reported as it arrives, and installing is a separate phase from ready, which
leaves the relaunch to an explicit "Restart now"; while bytes are in flight

The banner stops being an AlertDialog. It never needed a backdrop or a focus

fix(android): repair update checks and diagnostics export

The updater plugin is registered `#[cfg(desktop)]` and carries no Android
capability, so `check()` had no handler and every "Check for updates" ended
in an error toast. Sideloaded APKs now read the same `latest.json` the
desktop updater uses and hand the user to the release page; they cannot
install it themselves. The fetch runs in the Android plugin rather than
reqwest, which verifies through `rustls-platform-verifier` and would need a
JVM handshake this app never performs.

That check is gated on a build-time flag only the APK release job sets. A
Play Store build must not update itself outside Play's own mechanism, and
Play App Signing re-signs it, so those users could not install these APKs
over their copy anyway.

Saving diagnostics passed the SAF `content://` URI that Android's save
dialog returns to `std::fs::write` as if it were a path. The write failed
and left behind the 0-byte document `ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT` had just
created, which is the empty file in the report. It now goes through
ContentResolver. Showing the result afterwards was broken for the same
reason — the opener plugin has no Android support at all — so that is
best-effort and reuses the download-target intent chain.

Also drops a dead `meta.onError` from the periodic check: react-query only
invokes those via a QueryCache handler, which is not configured. Leaving
the unattended poll quiet is deliberate; the manual button still reports.

`IS_UPDATER_AVAILABLE` and gate both surfaces on it, so the check and

used to mount and call a `#[cfg(desktop)]` plugin that always rejected.

The banner now clears the footer instead of covering it — on a phone the
footer carries the safe-area inset, so the nav sat underneath it.

fix(history): stop Android rows pointing at app-private staging

Android receives into staging and only learns the real destination when
the export finishes, so recording the staging path at open left every
failed export — and every row written before `note_destination` existed
— offering an Open that resolves to a path no file manager can reach.
Leave `save_path` unset there and let the export fill it in.

Recorded names that are absolute or climb out of the destination are
ignored too. They cannot have come from the transfer, and they would
drag `resolve_open_target`'s common ancestor below the save path.
chore(release): bump version to 0.7.1

fix(pairing): stop nearby pair request flashing the no-code error

Accept sets `request` to null, which flips the dialog closed, but Base UI
keeps the popup mounted for its 200ms exit transition. VerificationCode
was rendered unguarded, so it took its `!code` branch during that window
and painted the red "couldn't compute a verification code" text before
unmounting.

Guard the render on `request`, matching NearbyInviteDialog — which got
the same guard in e3db53a, before the shared VerificationCode component
was extracted and this dialog was added without it.

fix(sender): fit the send-to-device sheet to the phone screen

Android is edge-to-edge, so the fixed inset-0 sheet ran under the status
and navigation bars: the header and close button sat behind the status
icons and the nav bar covered the bottom of the Nearby list. Sheets take
an opt-in safeArea prop that pads the popup (and offsets the close
button, which is placed against the padding box) per side.

The nearby list now shows 4 rows on phones and 3 from sm up, and the
sheet is 1rem narrower on phones with matching 1rem gutters instead of
1.5rem - the dismissable backdrop strip grows from 48 to 64px while the
content column keeps its width.

fix(ui): pad settings and history pages for the Android system bars

The settings pane fills the viewport on native, so its content ran to
the screen edge and the last row sat under the gesture bar; the history
header's pt-6 was shorter than the status bar, so the title rendered
behind it. Both now carry the safe-area insets the rest of the app
applies per surface.

The sidebar nav sheet padded top and bottom but not the horizontal
inset - it now pads its screen-facing edge too.

fix(history): stop offering to free partial data that is already gone

A row whose receive was interrupted keeps a pointer to its partial blob
store, and the history card offers to reclaim it. But the stat behind
that offer never checked the directory was still there — the name and
parent guard in `is_reclaimable_partial` both pass for a deleted path,
and `get_total_size` errors into `unwrap_or(0)`. Since the launch sweep
removes every `.dashbeam-recv-*` directory, each restart turned those
rows into a "Free up 0 B" button for space that was already free.

`stat_partial_store` now requires the directory to exist and to hold
bytes, so `exists` means "there is partial data worth reclaiming" — the
delete-confirm copy that quotes the same size gets the fix too. Rows are
also swept at launch: `forget_missing_partial_stores` drops pointers to
stores that are gone, stating each one so a store that survived a failed
sweep keeps its row's offer to free it.

fix(history): keep the row delete button on the last detail line

The button was pinned to the saved-to line, so a record without a save
path pushed it onto a line of its own below the details. Details are now
built as a list and the button rides whichever entry lands last, with
that entry widening when it would otherwise sit in the left column.

feat(history): refresh the list when a transfer lands while it is open

The page read the store once on mount, so a transfer arriving from a
trusted device stayed invisible until the user navigated away and back.

The recorder now announces `transfer-history-updated` whenever it writes
a terminal row or corrects a destination, and the page re-reads on it.
Announcing from the shell rather than listening for `receive-completed`
in the UI is what covers failed and cancelled receives: those finalize
their row without emitting any event the frontend could hear.
